items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Roy Eldridge joined the orchestra... it was an exciting pleasure to work with him and be in a position to hear him night after night.

ctx.x: One night in Pittsburgh I went to a club and was jamming with the musicians when a young boy 17 years old came in and took out an old trumpet that had no caps on the top of the valves. He did not have any experience and had not been playing long. But what he played there had plenty of fire in it

and I could tell that he was trying to play Rex Stewart's style of playing which was very fast. We started talking and he told me that his name was Roy Eldridge. He also told me that he was married and he was only 17. I don't know if it was true, but after I got to know Roy better, I believe that he could have been married because he was wild enough to do many things that most boys his age would not think of doing.

Shortly after we came back to Springfield from Pittsburgh, Bull William lost his father and inherited a model T Ford coupe. When we went on trips to different places Walker and I rode with Bull. The T Ford would run alright on a level road but when we came to a hill, if it was very long the radiator would heat up and steam would be coming from it like a puffing locomotive and we would have to stop and let it cool off.
